scientific_integrity.literature_risk: The 2019 Grebenkov work is highly relevant general first-passage theory; only its abstract and bibliographic information were accessible for comparison.
scientific_integrity.proof: The analytic proof gives exact survival representation, moments, algebraic inverse and strict feasible-region equivalence.
scientific_integrity.verification: Pure-Python independent spectral and reconstruction checks executed successfully; finite tests do not replace the proof.

scientific_limitations: The sharp inverse theorem holds for an exactly prepared reflecting–absorbing principal-mode spatial ensemble and a stationary symmetric two-state switching environment.
The interval size and arithmetic-mean diffusivity are assumed calibrated; the inverse has an unavoidable interchange of mobility labels.
No finite-sample, noise-stability, asymmetric-switching, general-initial-law, or multi-state result is claimed.
General switching-diffusion first-passage theory already supplies forward frameworks; historical priority of the particular inverse range theorem is not independently established.
title: Two absorption-time moments identify contrast and switching in a confined two-mobility diffusion
